reason: The text fragment consists entirely of the Joseph narrative in Egypt (Genesis 39-40), detailing Joseph's service in Potiphar's house, his imprisonment, and his interpretation of dreams for Pharaoh's officials. The passage repeatedly emphasizes God's continuous presence with and blessing upon Joseph individually (וַיְהִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ יוֹסֵ֔ף - 'the Lord was with Joseph'). The passage contains no reference whatsoever to God's relationship with Israel as a people, no discussion of divine loyalty or disloyalty toward the covenant people, and no indication that God considers replacing them with another people. The statement concerns God's relationship to the collective people, while this text addresses only God's favor toward one individual.
